PRECONDITION vs DELIVERABLE (artifact kind: impl-plan) — a plan PROPOSES changes; it has not run.
Verify only that its PRECONDITIONS hold against the live repo:
  • the anchor / insertion-point text each edit attaches to EXISTS (verbatim);
  • assumed-existing files, symbols, and signatures are present;
  • the described edits would apply and compose.
The plan's PROPOSED new code, new tests, comment edits, and version bumps are its
DELIVERABLE — they are EXPECTED to be absent from the current repo. NEVER report
their absence as a finding. Only a missing or changed ANCHOR / PRECONDITION —
something an edit needs in order to land — is a defect.
A false claim about EXISTING code, a wrong signature, a drifted line number, or an internal contradiction remains a real finding.
If you nonetheless surface an expected-absence finding (the "absent" symbol is a plan DELIVERABLE mapped by the coverage-vs-source lens to a plan task), set that finding's deliverableAbsence:true so the gate scores it as expected work, never a blocker.

Apply the red-team backstop-legitimacy check and the judge-tag grading rule to the plan (repo: /Users/ljf/GitHub/WorkAuditRefine/.claude/worktrees/codex-red-team-migration-5ca53a). For EACH entry in '## Deferred validations (backstops)' (B1, B2): (i) is 'why deferred' a concrete reason the check cannot run pre-merge, not a bare 'later'? (ii) does a cheaper deterministic pre-merge proxy already cover part of it (then it is over-broad and must narrow — e.g. does B1 defer anything that Task 2's offline actual-host cases or package tests already prove)? (iii) are runner AND timing named? A failure on any → a needsDecision finding. Then for each End state carrying `judge:`/`HARD at audit_sha` (End state 6) or `backstop:` (End state 7), grade: could this have been a `check:` command? For End state 6, note the plan's own rationale (ledger evidence links sampled against actual history) and decide whether at least a partial mechanical check (e.g. the ledger file exists, has the required sections, and every relative evidence link resolves) is commandable — if so, is the fully-judged form box-ticking, or justified? Commandable-but-judged → needsDecision. Also grade End states 1–5: each cites `node --test <new test file>` as its check — is a not-yet-written test file a discriminating check for the stated condition, or could a trivially-green test satisfy it? Report whether the plan's Validation-interpretation clause ('Deterministic fixtures must independently state expected behavior and include failure controls') plus the enumerated fixture scenarios in Task 1/Task 2 make the checks discriminating, or whether a specific End state remains satisfiable by a vacuous test (a Major). Read-only; findings only for actual defects.

Return ONLY the FINDINGS object (probe="backstop-legitimacy-judge", kind="bespoke", technique="analyzed"). Prove any failure with reproduced evidence; never assert. Set needsDecision:true on any finding that is an ambiguity with more than one non-equivalent resolution — a hole only the user can settle. Only record a finding for an actual problem — a false claim, a gap, or an ambiguity (needsDecision). If a claim checks out, do NOT record it. A fully-clean probe returns status:"pass" with findings:[].
